msg: Card verification code column. Sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorisation, even encrypted.
fix: Drop the column and read the code from the gateway request in memory only.

msg: Full track / magnetic-stripe equivalent data. This is sensitive authentication data and may never be retained after authorisation.
fix: Remove the column; keep only the token the processor returns.

msg: PIN or PIN block column. Sensitive authentication data must not be stored after authorisation.
fix: Remove the column. PIN translation belongs in the HSM, never in a table.

msg: Primary account number stored in a readable column type. Stored PAN must be rendered unreadable wherever it is kept.
fix: Store a network token or a keyed hash, plus first6/last4 in their own columns.

msg: Index or key built on the account number itself, which keeps the PAN readable and searchable in the index pages.
fix: Index the token or the keyed hash column instead.

msg: Card data written into a log, audit or history table. Log stores are rarely in scope for key management and are copied everywhere.
fix: Log the token and the last four digits only.

msg: Whole authorisation payload kept as a blob. These bodies routinely carry the PAN and the verification code, so the column inherits every rule above.
fix: Persist named fields you have reviewed, or redact the payload before insert.

msg: View exposes the full account number. When PAN is displayed it must be masked to at most the first six and last four digits.
fix: Wrap the column: 'XXXXXX' || RIGHT(card_ref, 4) AS card_display.

msg: Luhn-valid account number written straight into the migration. A card number in version control is card data in every clone, backup and CI log.
fix: Seed with a processor test token, or a number that is not Luhn-valid.

msg: Table holds card data but defines no retention or purge column, so nothing tells you when the row may be deleted.
fix: Add purge_after DATE (or retain_until) and a scheduled delete that reads it.
